title: Fabrik — agent harness for parallel software delivery
desc: A harness in which worker agents turn tickets into pull requests in parallel ([fabrikhq.com](https://fabrikhq.com)). A **control plane** (FastAPI, Vue) spawns one agent container per repository through the Docker socket. Each agent runs a fixed loop — ticket sync (GitHub, GitLab, Jira), an actionability review that rejects vague tickets, a plan, test-first implementation, a **quality gate** in a clean sidecar container, then the PR; it never merges on its own. Energy budget per agent, feedback from PR comments back into the loop, one VPS per customer behind Caddy.

title: Autonomous coding pipeline — agents work a task queue unattended
desc: Queue-driven harness in which coding agents work through tasks with nobody at the keyboard. A task file names repository, scope, acceptance criteria and model; a runner on own hardware executes it in an isolated worktree, runs the **quality gate** (unit tests, build, review) before any push and opens a pull request — merging stays with a human. Model chosen per task against a 5-hour token budget, hard timeouts per run, at most one new pull request per repository per night. **759 tasks** written to date across the own product repositories.

title: Autonomous AI business partner — Harness & agentic engineering
desc: A self-directing agent built on Claude that plans, writes code, tests, deploys and reports around the clock. Built as a **harness engineer** — the engineering around the model: the **agent loop** and its stop conditions, **tool use over MCP**, layered **memory** (durable facts, running context, session state), **approval gates** for anything irreversible, **observability** over every run, **budget and rate-limit control** with model routing, plus recovery when a run is killed mid-flight. More than 40 purpose-built checks catch the agent's mistakes before they reach a human. Event-driven over Telegram, GitHub and systemd; runs on own hardware behind a local multi-model proxy.

title: Verification and drift controls for LLM agents
desc: More than 40 purpose-built checks that test an agent's work against the world instead of against its own report: every link in an outgoing message is resolved before it is sent, promises the agent made are tracked until delivered, messages without an answer are flagged, pull-request mergeability is computed with git instead of read from a cached API value, and a test run that never started fails instead of passing silently. Each check fails closed — unknown is never reported as healthy — and has its own tests. Watchdogs over the agent's services and credentials, with a second alert path for when the primary channel is the one that broke.

title: LLM agent in the finance back office of a GmbH
desc: An agent that runs the bookkeeping of a German GmbH end to end, with a human approving every filing. It files bank statements and receipts, books double-entry on SKR04 through a purpose-built CLI, reconciles every account against the statement, and checks VAT and payroll returns against the journal before they are submitted — once catching a field that would have lost the input tax. Tools beneath it: an API for **XRechnung 3.0** and **ZUGFeRD 2.3** with five validation layers (Pydantic, BR-DE rules, arithmetic, XSD, Schematron), balance sheet, P&L, E-Bilanz and **DATEV export**.

title: Launch Kit — multi-tenant identity and email platform
desc: OIDC-compliant auth server with email marketing as one Go binary and a Vue admin UI — a drop-in for Keycloak or Auth0. **OAuth2 with PKCE**, RS256 JWTs with a per-tenant RSA key, Login with Google, role-based access. Contacts, segments and campaigns with async sending, unsubscribe handling and GDPR consent. Strict tenant isolation; apps validate tokens over JWKS only and swap the provider by changing an environment variable. Runs the customer funnel of several own products.

title: Paid browser extensions — FinGrab, PlaylistGrab, InvoiceGrab
desc: A portfolio of browser extensions for Chrome (MV3) and Firefox from one codebase with WXT and TypeScript; FinGrab exports market data from Yahoo Finance as CSV and has around 600 users. **Live payments** through ExtPay and Stripe, subscription and one-time purchase. End-to-end tests with Playwright against the built package, a regression diff against the shipped version, publishing over the API to the Chrome Web Store and addons.mozilla.org, monitoring of reviews, subscriptions and the paywall.

title: Digital property profile for owners
desc: Full-stack development of a digital property profile that owners create and maintain themselves: Vue.js front-end, Python back-end (Eve) with a REST API and MongoDB. Built and maintained the GitLab CI pipelines for automated build and deployment. Worked to DevOps principles, owning build and operation of the services in Docker. Test-driven development, automated end-to-end tests with Playwright.

title: Front- and back-end, heating cost billing
desc: Production server-side services and APIs in Java and Spring Boot: a microservice that parses and generates heating-cost files in the Haweiko-Arge industry format. Designed and built in a microservices architecture with REST interfaces (OpenAPI, Swagger), secured with Spring Security and Keycloak, persisted in MongoDB. Built and maintained the GitLab CI pipelines for automated build and deployment. Worked to DevOps principles, owning build and operation of the services in Docker. Test-driven development (JUnit, Mockito), automated end-to-end tests with Playwright. Front-end development.

title: Payment back-end migration Java EE → Spring Boot
desc: Migrated an EJB-based Java EE payment back-end to Spring Boot and shipped it as a Docker container.

title: Software and data analysis in marketing
desc: Server-side services in Java and Spring Boot: web-scraping microservices plus microsites (Vue.js, Quasar) with a Spring Boot back-end for calculators, surveys and questionnaire funnels; data analysis in R. Designed and built in a microservices architecture with REST interfaces (OpenAPI, Feign), persisted in PostgreSQL and MongoDB. Built and maintained the GitLab CI pipelines. Worked to DevOps principles, owning build and operation of the services in Docker and Kubernetes.

title: Marketing campaign tooling
desc: Tools that generate marketing campaigns and publish them to Google Ads and Twitter Ads: Java/Spring Boot microservices with REST interfaces (OpenAPI, Feign), Vue.js/Quasar front-end, storage in AWS S3. Designed and built in a microservices architecture. Built and maintained the GitLab CI pipelines. Worked to DevOps principles, owning build and operation of the services in Docker and Kubernetes.

title: Web-based configuration of telecommunications devices
desc: Took over an existing prototype for configuring telecommunications devices over a web interface, developed it further and moved it into production. Production server-side services and APIs in Java and Spring Boot in a microservices architecture (REST, Feign, Spring Data/JPA), Vue.js front-end, secured with Keycloak, persisted in MySQL and MongoDB. Worked to DevOps principles, owning build, operation and monitoring of the services: Docker and Kubernetes (Rancher), logging and tracing via Kibana, Sleuth and Zipkin; built and maintained the GitLab CI pipelines.

title: Training a stock-trading agent
desc: An agent that trades autonomously on Chinese stock exchanges (reinforcement learning).

title: Data analysis and modelling at a consumer cooperative
desc: Exploratory data analysis, data cleaning, aggregation; unsupervised learning (clustering, feature reduction).

title: Image homogeneity of product niches from product photos
desc: A model that quantifies the image homogeneity of Amazon product niches to spot under-served niches early. Trained a ResNet50 CNN with transfer learning (Keras) and deployed it through a build pipeline as a Java microservice with DeepLearning4J into the existing landscape; prepared a Kafka data pipeline for continuous retraining.

title: Aesthetic classification of Airbnb photos
desc: A microservice that scores the quality of Airbnb photos: a Python scraper built an image database (~15k images), labelling via Amazon Mechanical Turk, exploratory data analysis in R; trained a CNN with transfer learning (Keras, ResNet50) on an AWS GPU instance and deployed it as a Spring Boot microservice with DeepLearning4J.

title: Connected Van — driver's logbook
desc: Microservices for vehicle geolocation and a fuel logbook.

desc: Platform covering the full invoice life cycle (creation, payment, dunning, debt collection); a range of Spring Boot microservices.

desc: Implementation of business services as part of the re-build of a booking and reservation system.

desc: Money transfer between accounts by scanning a QR code; hybrid app (GWT) embedded in native mobile apps for broad platform coverage.
